questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1-Hexanol is treated with Infrared absorption spectrometer?

options.label: A
options.text: C=O stretch at 1735 cm-1 and strong C-O stretch at 1240 cm-1

options.label: C
options.text: Twin molecular ion peaks at m/z = 122 and 124 (1:1 ratio)

options.label: D
options.text: Sharp peak at 3300 cm-1 and weak peak at 2120 cm-1

questions.explanation: Treating 1-Hexanol with Infrared absorption spectrometer yields Broad, strong peak at 3300-3400 cm-1. Rationale: Hydrogen-bonded O-H stretching vibration produces a characteristically broad, intense absorption.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 2-Pentanone into Strong, sharp peak at 1715 cm-1?
questions.explanation: To convert 2-Pentanone into Strong, sharp peak at 1715 cm-1, the appropriate reagent is Infrared absorption spectrometer. Rationale: Unconjugated aliphatic carbonyl (C=O) stretching produces a sharp, prominent absorption band.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Sharp peak at 3300 cm-1 and weak peak at 2120 cm-1

questions.correct_answer: Sharp peak at 3300 cm-1 and weak peak at 2120 cm-1
questions.explanation: Treating 1-Hexyne with Infrared absorption spectrometer yields Sharp peak at 3300 cm-1 and weak peak at 2120 cm-1. Rationale: Terminal sp C-H stretch appears as a sharp band at 3300 cm-1; C≡C stretch appears near 2120 cm-1.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Butanenitrile into Medium sharp peak at 2250 cm-1?
questions.explanation: To convert Butanenitrile into Medium sharp peak at 2250 cm-1, the appropriate reagent is Infrared absorption spectrometer. Rationale: Carbon-nitrogen triple bond (C≡N) stretching produces a sharp absorption band in the 2200-2300 cm-1 region.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Acetone (C3H6O, M+ = 58) is treated with Electron ionization mass spectrometer?

options.label: A
options.text: Sharp peak at 3300 cm-1 and weak peak at 2120 cm-1

options.label: C
options.text: Twin molecular ion peaks at m/z = 122 and 124 (1:1 ratio)

questions.explanation: Treating Acetone (C3H6O, M+ = 58) with Electron ionization mass spectrometer yields Base peak at m/z = 43 (Acylium ion [CH3CO]+). Rationale: Alpha-cleavage of a methyl radical leaves the resonance-stabilized acylium cation (m/z 43).

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 2-Hexanone (C6H12O, M+ = 100) into Prominent fragment at m/z = 58 + Neutral propene?
questions.explanation: To convert 2-Hexanone (C6H12O, M+ = 100) into Prominent fragment at m/z = 58 + Neutral propene, the appropriate reagent is Electron ionization mass spectrometer. Rationale: Gamma-hydrogen transfer via a 6-membered transition state cleaves the alpha-beta bond, expelling propene.

questions.explanation: Treating 2-Hexanone (C6H12O, M+ = 100) with Electron ionization mass spectrometer yields Prominent fragment at m/z = 58 + Neutral propene. Rationale: Gamma-hydrogen transfer via a 6-membered transition state cleaves the alpha-beta bond, expelling propene.
